newsitem.title: GERMANY: Small Audi shareholders beef about dividend.
newsitem.headline: Small Audi shareholders beef about dividend.

text.p: Some of the few remaining individual shareholders in carmaker Audi AG complained on Wednesday that parent company Volkswagen AG was "plundering" the luxury carmaker at their expense.
Despite record sales and profits at Audi, some of the individual shareholders told the carmaker's annual general meeting that dividend payments must be raised.
Audi, which is 99 percent owned by VW, paid a 1996 dividend of nine marks per share, up from six marks in 1995.
One shareholder said he was considering whether to file a lawsuit against Audi over the dividend policy and called on the carmaker to revise its profit-transfer pact with VW.
Audi, which had a 1996 pre-tax profit of 862 million marks, said it would transfer 125 million marks to VW in 1996, up from 80 million marks in 1995.
